Authors: Frank van Eekeren, Chris Noij, Gerolf Pikker

Source: Sport in Society

Why included: Canadian-affiliated author or institution

Abstract: This paper examines how ethical reflexivity can deepen our understanding of contract researcher strategies and collaborative governance in Sport for Development (SFD). Drawing on a critical incident from our role as contract researchers in a Dutch-led SFD program, we explore how ethical tensions emerge from conflicting institutional expectations, personal values, and unequal power relations between actors from the Global North and South. Rather than offering definitive solutions, the study presents ethical reflexivity as a situated practice. Practically, it enables researchers to navigate ambiguity and make sense of tensions as they arise. Epistemologically, it sheds light on the everyday micro-practices that shape collaborative governance.
